text:
Field and sea, so joined in one canticle,
man has found only rarely in the world.
Sailor and farmer, together;
with earth and net, a single trade.

The sowed fields of sea and land
offer themselves to one family.
The blue meadows of the waters,
and the soft earth the sun drinks in.

A single gaze takes in the whole:
the miracle of bread and fish.
The shepherd walks upon the waters,
and the tree of his cross grows close by.

Palms in flocks, carob trees,
olives and almond groves, pomegranates
shelter the one who eats from the waters,
mixing sea salt with dark oil.

Oh land of this sea, red and deep,
flowering with mills and saltworks!
I transcend the perpetual architecture
of your being and not-doing, your living force!

translation.title: Field and Sea, So Joined in a Canticle…
translation.editorial_note: Translated from the stored Spanish original. The fusion of farming, fishing, landscape, and Christian bread-and-fish imagery is preserved.
